tagline: Across the Muskingum, with old work close by.
intro: From Bishopville, laid out in 1859 on the south side of Burr Oak State Park, Route 78 reaches Ringgold and runs on to the Muskingum River. Malta stands on the west bank and McConnelsville on the east, and the route crosses between them on its way toward Meigs.

Malta took its name from an early settler who had seen the island as a sailor. Both towns grew on river trade after locks and dams went into the Muskingum between 1836 and 1841, and the 1913 bridge between them is part of the river's historic navigation district. Covered and iron bridges turn up elsewhere along the byway too.

moments.title: Bishopville
moments.text: The community stands beside Burr Oak State Park's southern edge, where it has a public dock.

moments.title: Malta
moments.text: The Morgan County Dungeon, a stone jail about 11 feet long and 5 wide, once held people convicted of larceny, rioting and adultery; rediscovered in 1964, it now sits on Main Street.

moments.title: McConnelsville
moments.text: Built in 1892 on the public square, the opera house was one of the first buildings in the county lit by electricity, and William Jennings Bryan spoke from its stage.
